- 2026-07-23: Added atomic aggregate reads to canonical GC returned-value evidence. `struct.atomic.get` and `array.atomic.get` already share declared field/element typing with ordinary aggregate reads, but the value-slice stack model omitted their operand arities and the terminal result classifier omitted their typed result paths. Both atomic families now preserve their complete object/object-plus-index slices and derive reference candidates through the existing struct/array type helpers. - 2026-07-23: Added typed `local.tee` to canonical GC returned-value evidence. The returned-value slice already preserved terminal local-write side effects and knew the local's stack shape, but the terminal instruction classifier recognized only `local.get`, causing an otherwise representable `local.get -> local.tee` leaf result to fail refinement. `local.tee` now derives the same declared-local candidate type without rewriting or removing the write. A red-first nonnullable leaf-to-nullable-base slice regression proves the side-effecting carrier participates. Bounded validation passes at validator typecheck `551/551`, DAE white-box `379/379`, public DAE/DAEO `340/340`, pass-manager `305/305`, and `moon info` with zero errors.
- 2026-07-23: Resolved owner-relative recursive-group supertypes in DAE GC LUB traversal. - 2026-06-28: Broadened OI-G live atomic RMW dynamic end-byte evidence under the existing `oi-live-nonzero-memory-atomic-rmw-boundary` grouped workflow. A red-first extension of `src/fuzz/metamorphic_wbtest.mbt::OI live nonzero memory-atomic RMW boundary transform guards reachable integer RMW variants` failed until `src/fuzz/metamorphic.mbt` emitted a guarded dynamic end-byte `memory.size * 65536 - 1` byte-width atomic sequence for memory32 and memory64-only modules. Grouped `.tmp/oi-g-live-atomic-rmw-end-byte-count130-20260628` compared 130/130 with 108 normalized matches, 22 mismatches, zero validation/generator/property/command failures, and Binaryen cache hits/misses 125/5; `--summarize-existing` confirmed the same result. The broadened atomic RMW/store/cmpxchg transform and prior atomic-load transform each sampled ten cases and all ten matched. ## [2026-06-24] passes/optimize-instructions | Re-enable guarded commutative canonicalization and document reorder contracts

- Made the leading-rewrite soundness contract precise across the optimize-instructions wiki: the leading `(0 - x) + y -> y - x` rewrite reorders the two value computations and is gated by `optimize_instructions_subtrees_can_swap` (no RAW/WAR/WAW region conflict on locals/globals/memory/tables; no may-trap/throw operand past a side effect; no control-flow operands), mirroring Binaryen's reorder rule. The trailing `y + (0 - x) -> y - x` needs no guard. The sibling `-x * -y -> x * y` strips both `(0 - x)` wrappers in place, so it needs no reorder proof and applies even for effectful factors such as `(0 - call) * (0 - y)`.
- Re-enabled `optimize_instructions_try_canonicalize_commutative` for ranked non-call HOT value nodes using the same `subtrees_can_swap` proof, restoring safe canonicalization for leading constants, local-get ordering, and nested expression/local ordering while keeping same-region local/memory conflicts, may-trap past side-effect hazards, and control-flow operands blocked. `HotOp::Call`/`CallIndirect`/`CallRef` still carry no kind rank, so general call-operand commutative ordering remains a follow-up slice.
- Updated `src/passes/optimize_instructions.mbt`, `src/passes/optimize_instructions_test.mbt`, `binaryen/passes/optimize-instructions/{wat-shapes,binaryen-strategy,starshine-strategy,starshine-hot-ir-strategy}.md`, and `agent-todo.md`. - Filed [`raw/research/1085-2026-06-25-heap-store-optimization-control-scan-skip.md`](raw/research/1085-2026-06-25-heap-store-optimization-control-scan-skip.md). `hso_process_node_regions(...)` now skips recursive pre-pass region descent for subtrees whose effect mask has no HOT control, leaving the current-region `local.set` / `struct.set` chain scan unchanged. Focused HSO tests passed (`416/416`), `moon fmt` passed, native `src/cmd` build passed with pre-existing unused-function warnings, and a 1000-case direct HSO compare normalized `1000/1000` with `0` mismatches/failures. Allocation-heavy Starshine HSO medians improved from `5.904ms` to `5.612ms` at 1000 functions and from `11.988ms` to `11.199ms` at 2000 functions, but HSO-I remains open because the fixture is still `~5.3x` slower than Binaryen at 2000 functions.

## [2026-06-25] passes/heap-store-optimization | Profile allocation-heavy HSO scaling

- Filed [`raw/research/1084-2026-06-25-heap-store-optimization-allocation-heavy-scaling.md`](raw/research/1084-2026-06-25-heap-store-optimization-allocation-heavy-scaling.md). Generated 250/500/1000-function siblings of the allocation-heavy HSO fixture and measured three Starshine traced runs plus three Binaryen `--debug` pass-local runs for each. All emitted wasm files validated. Starshine HSO pass-local medians were `1.597ms`, `2.962ms`, and `5.904ms`; Binaryen medians were `0.186ms`, `0.503ms`, and `0.791ms`. Together with `1072` at 2000 functions (`11.988ms` vs `2.110ms`), the slowdown is roughly linear and HSO-owned, not just fixed startup or no-candidate O4z artifact overhead. HSO-I remains open; likely next targets are the pre-rewrite recursive region scan, per-function cache allocation, and repeated simple-shape safety predicates.

## [2026-06-20] passes/heap-store-optimization | Fix descriptor later-field global writes

- Filed [`raw/research/0861-2026-06-20-heap-store-optimization-descriptor-later-field-global-write.md`](raw/research/0861-2026-06-20-heap-store-optimization-descriptor-later-field-global-write.md). Fixed a Binaryen parity gap where Starshine kept `struct.set` for descriptor constructors whose later field wrote one mutable global while the moved value read or wrote an unrelated global. ## [2026-06-20] passes/heap-store-optimization | Fix external-exit control folds

- Filed [`raw/research/0797-2026-06-20-heap-store-optimization-external-exits.md`](raw/research/0797-2026-06-20-heap-store-optimization-external-exits.md). Local Binaryen `version_130` probes showed HSO folds conditional external `throw` and `return_call` set values into `struct.new`, and also folds a conditional `return_call` inside active `try_table`; conditional `throw` inside an active catch remains a negative follow-up. Starshine previously retained `struct.set` for the three positives because `return_call*` / `throw*` were classified as skipped-local-set hazards and `return_call*` was treated as an active-catch escape. HSO now treats those terminators as function-external exits for skip-local-set purposes, keeps `unreachable` as a no-fold boundary, and removes `return_call*` from active-catch escape blocking while ordinary `call*` / `throw*` still block there. Focused HSO tests passed `81/81`, `moon info`, `moon fmt`, `moon test src/passes` `2709/2709`, full `moon test` `6022/6022`, native `src/cmd` build passed with existing warnings, and direct 10000-case compare `.tmp/pass-fuzz-heap-store-optimization-external-exits-10000` compared `10000/10000` with `10000` normalized matches, `0` mismatches, and `0` command/validation/property/generator failures. Broader in-function branch/catch negatives remain open.

## [2026-06-20] passes/heap-store-optimization | Fix disappearing-bad-get control fold

- Filed [`raw/research/0796-2026-06-20-heap-store-optimization-disappearing-bad-get.md`](raw/research/0796-2026-06-20-heap-store-optimization-disappearing-bad-get.md). Binaryen `version_130` folds the exact `control-flow-in-set-value-sequence-yes` case where a branch-valued `struct.set` can move into the constructor because the only bad target-local read is inside the skipped owner tail and no outside read follows the dropped block. Starshine now tracks owner-external roots during nested HSO traversal and allows a branch-only root immediately before a matching later `struct.set` to move before the delayed fresh-struct `local.set` only when the target local is not touched after the owner expression. [`binaryen/passes/remove-unused-brs/implementation-structure-and-tests.md`](binaryen/passes/remove-unused-brs/implementation-structure-and-tests.md), [`binaryen/passes/remove-unused-brs/parity.md`](binaryen/passes/remove-unused-brs/parity.md), [`binaryen/passes/remove-unused-brs/select-and-condition-rewrites.md`](binaryen/passes/remove-unused-brs/select-and-condition-rewrites.md), and [`../../agent-todo.md`](../../agent-todo.md) now record that Starshine has no expression-level `metadata.code.branch_hint` representation, parser/lowerer path, binary code-metadata section, or RUB remap target. Binaryen `BranchHints::copyTo`, `copyFlippedTo`, `applyAndTo`, `applyOrTo`, `flip`, and `clear` therefore remain unsupported metadata preservation until a dedicated code-metadata implementation lands.
- The same boundary covers Binaryen `remove-unused-brs-never-unconditionalize`: Starshine currently has no `--pass-arg` / pass-option equivalent, so condition-combining, selectifying, and restructuring RUB rewrites are ordinary direct-pass behavior rather than configurable never-unconditionalize parity. Reopening requires a code-metadata representation plus parser/lowerer/binary or opaque-section policy, branch-hint remap tests, and explicit pass-option tests for the guarded rewrites. `[O4Z-AUDIT-RUB-K]` selectify remains open, so `[O4Z-AUDIT-RUB-O]` final closeout is not claimed.

## [2026-05-24] fuzzing | FUZ1034 GenValid PRNG stream split batch migration

- Continued `[FUZ]1034` by adding `gen_valid_module_result_from_seed(...)`, an explicit root-seed GenValid entry point that derives named candidate substreams instead of consuming one monolithic `RandomState`.
- The first migrated streams route function type/result/local choices through the `types` stream and body statement counts through the `bodies` stream, while preserving the legacy `RandomState` API for callers that need old seed behavior.
- GenValid batch emitters now use the root-seed API per candidate so batch manifests' existing `stream_derivations` describe real generation choices, and focused tests lock type-choice stability when only the body budget changes.
- Continued the migration by moving function-count and function-signature assignment onto the `funcs` stream, memory/table/data/element counts and local shape choices onto their matching streams, and keeping the metadata-budget stability test green for single-attempt generated candidates.
- Continued the stream-map audit by adding dedicated `globals`, `tags`, and `start` stream labels to GenValid manifests, then routing defined-global counts, global reference/type/init choices, defined-tag counts, and start-section rollout through those streams instead of the module-topology fallback.
- Continued the named-stream migration by moving invalid-AST base-module generation onto per-strategy/per-seed-profile seeds derived from the `invalid-mutation-choice` stream. Each invalid strategy now gets a stable GenValid root seed independent of neighboring strategy scheduling, and the seeded generation path reuses `gen_valid_module_result_from_seed(...)` instead of advancing one shared monolithic `RandomState` across the whole invalid-AST run.
- Continued the named-stream migration by deriving GenValid batch candidate root seeds from the `harness-shuffling` stream before per-candidate salting, replacing the previous direct `seed ^ index` batch path while preserving deterministic candidate order and manifest stream labels.
- Added a manifest stream-derivation roundtrip helper for `[FUZ]1034` so `stream_derivations` can be parsed back into stable `{ label, derived_seed }` records, and locked the harness-shuffling derived seed with a focused whitebox test.
- Continued the repro-audit slice by exposing `validate_invalid_text_dynamic_stream_seed(...)` and recording the dynamic invalid-text `text-mutation-choice` stream label plus derived stream seed in suite detail JSON, so dynamic GenValid-WAT failures can cite the owning named PRNG stream directly.
- Continued the persisted-repro audit by adding optional stream-label/stream-seed fields to `InvalidFuzzFailureReport`; AST and binary invalid repro builders now persist the `invalid-mutation-choice` stream label plus derived stream seed, and metadata parse/load roundtrips preserve those fields.
- Continued the attempt-level repro audit by adding optional `attempt_seed` metadata to `InvalidFuzzFailureReport`; AST and binary invalid repro builders now persist the exact per-strategy/profile GenValid root seed, and the binary invalid runner now derives attempts from the same `invalid-mutation-choice` stream plus stable strategy/profile salts instead of advancing one monolithic binary invalid `RandomState`.
- Signed off `[FUZ]1034`: GenValid batch manifests now expose named stream derivations, generated valid modules use split substreams for topology/type/function/body/memory/table/data/element/global/tag/start choices, invalid AST/binary and dynamic text lanes cite their owning mutation streams, and persisted AST/binary repros include the exact attempt seed needed to replay the interesting generated specimen.

## [2026-04-10] maintain | collapse tuple seed screening into one precise scan and cut full-artifact pass time

- Reworked `src/passes/tuple_optimization.mbt` so tuple-opt no longer runs a weak whole-function no-op screen in `run`, repeats that same weak screen in `analyze`, and then pays a second seed walk anyway. The pass now builds or reuses `use-def`, performs one precise seed-group scan, bails out immediately when that scan is empty, and reuses the collected groups for the rest of analysis.
- Tightened the seed, result-block, and scalar-forward collectors themselves to avoid the old per-candidate GC churn: they now use stamped local marks for duplicate-lane detection and write lane order directly instead of building temporary reverse arrays and calling `tuple_optimization_seen_local(...)` linearly on every lane.
- Added focused white-box invariants in `src/passes/tuple_optimization_wbtest.mbt` proving that duplicate lane locals in both seed groups and result-block copy groups are still rejected under the new stamped-mark collectors.
- Rechecked correctness on the kept tree: `moon test --package jtenner/starshine/passes --file tuple_optimization_wbtest.mbt` is `44 / 44`, `moon test --package jtenner/starshine/cmd --file cmd_native_wbtest.mbt --target native --filter '*tuple-optimization*'` is `15 / 15`, `moon test --package jtenner/starshine/cmd --file cmd_wbtest.mbt --filter '*tuple-optimization*'` is `7 / 7`, `/tmp/pass-fuzz-tuple-cleaned-genvalid-1000-2026-04-10` is `1000 / 1000`, and `/tmp/pass-fuzz-tuple-cleaned-smith-200-2026-04-10` is `199 / 200` with the same Binaryen-only `binaryen-rec-group-zero` command failure.
- The full-artifact runtime moved materially, not just the reduced repros. `/tmp/self-opt-tuple-full-candidatefilter-2026-04-10` and `/tmp/self-opt-tuple-full-candidatefilter-rerun-2026-04-10` are both canonically green (`Canonical function compare equal: yes`, `Normalized WAT equal: yes`) while Starshine tuple-pass time dropped into a `325.221-361.452 ms` band from the earlier `~966 ms` band.
- Fresh pass-trace evidence explains why the improvement is real: tuple-opt still visits `4462` functions but now changes only `18`, and total pass time on the cleaned kept tree is `277790 us` instead of `960971 us`, so the old unchanged-function hot quartet is gone and the remaining runtime debt is concentrated in `Func 1673` plus a smaller tail of candidate-heavy functions.
- The current kept-tree split is now sharper too: `Func 1673` (`_M0FP37jtenner9starshine4wast17wt__lower__module`) is still the main tuple-pass outlier at `101831 us`, followed by a much smaller tail (`148`, `2389`, `1905`, `3660`, `147`), while the biggest `analysis:use-def` costs are still in different functions (`3612`, `1553`, `1525`). That means the next tuple-runtime slice should target `Func 1673`-style candidate/query work, while any wall-time reduction beyond the reported tuple pass timer will need separate use-def or pipeline work.
